farraa:1-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلنَّازِعَاتِ غَرْقاً﴾ to the end of the verses.
It is mentioned that they are the angels, and that the drawing out (النزع) is drawing the souls out of the breasts of the disbelievers. It is like your saying: والنازعات إغراقاً (by those who draw to the utmost), just as the archer draws the bow to the full (يُغرِق). Similar to it is: ﴿وَٱلنَّاشِطَاتِ نَشْطاً﴾. It is said that they take the soul of the believer as the hobble is loosened (يُنشَط) from the camel. What I have heard from the Arabs is that they say: أنشطتُ (I loosened), and "as though he had been loosened (أُنشِط) from a hobble"; and tying it is نشطها. So when you tie the rope on the camel's foreleg you are ناشط, and when you untie it you have أنشطته, and you are منشط.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلسَّابِحَاتِ سَبْحاً﴾.
The angels also; He made their descent from heaven like swimming. The Arabs say of the excellent horse [124/a]: إنه لسابح (it is a swimmer), when it passes stretching itself.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱلسَّابِقَاتِ سَبْقاً﴾.
They are the angels who outstrip the devils in bringing the revelation to the prophets, since the devils used to eavesdrop.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱلْمُدَبِّرَاتِ أَمْراً﴾.
They are the angels also; they descend with the lawful and the unlawful, and that is their arranging (تدبير) — though it belongs to Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He; but since they descended with it, they were called by that, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿نَزَلَ بِهِ الرُّوحُ الأَمِينُ﴾, and as He said: ﴿فَإِنَّهُ نَزَّلَهُ عَلَى قَلْبِكَ﴾, meaning: Gabriel, peace be upon him, brought it down upon the heart of Muhammad, may Allah bless them both and grant them peace, while it is Allah who sent it down. The questioner may ask: Where is the response (jawāb) to the oath in al-Nāziʿāt? It is one of those whose response is left out because the hearers know it. The meaning — as though, had it been overt, it would be: لتُبعثُنّ ولتُحاسَبُنّ (you will surely be resurrected and you will surely be called to account). What indicates that is their saying: "When we are decayed bones?" Do you not see that it is like a reply to His [implied] saying: "You will surely be resurrected", since they said: "When we are decayed bones, will we be resurrected?"

farraa:6-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ ٱلرَّاجِفَةُ﴾.
It is the first blowing [of the Trumpet]. ﴿تَتْبَعُهَا ٱلرَّادِفَةُ﴾: it is the second blowing.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلْحَافِرَةِ﴾.
It is said: [back] to our first state, to life. The Arabs say: أتيت فلاناً ثم رجعت على حافرتي (I came to So-and-so, then went back on my tracks), i.e. I returned to where I came from. Of that is the Arabs' saying: النقد عند الحافرة (payment at the very first moment). Its meaning: when he says "I have sold it to you", I come back to him with the price; and both are the same in meaning. Some say: النقد عند الحافر. He said: I asked one of the Arabs about it, and he said: النقد عند الحافر, meaning: at the hoof of the horse; as though this proverb arose concerning horses.
Some said: الحافرة is the ground in which their graves are dug, so He called it الحافرة, the meaning being المحفورة (the dug [ground]), just as it was said: ماء دافق (gushing water), meaning: مدفوق (poured out).

farraa:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿أَإِذَا كُنَّا عِظَاماً نَّاخِرَةً﴾. Al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to me from al-Suddī from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, who said: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb reading: "إِذا كُنَّا عِظَاماً نَاخِرَةً". Al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: al-Kisāʾī narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl from ʿAṭāʾ from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān from ʿAlī, may Allah have mercy on him, that he read "نَخِرَةً"; and he claimed in this isnad of his that Ibn ʿAbbās read it "نخرة". [Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us], saying: Sharīk ibn ʿAbdullāh and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Taymī Abū Saʿīd narrated to me from Mughīra from Mujāhid. Sharīk said: Ibn ʿAbbās read "عظاما ناخرة". Muḥammad said, with his isnad from Mughīra from Mujāhid: He said: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr saying on the pulpit: "What is the matter with boys who read (نخرة), when it is only (ناخرة)?" [Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us [124/b], saying: Mindal narrated to me from Layth from Mujāhid from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read: (ناخرة). The people of Medina and al-Ḥasan read: (نخرة). (ناخرة) is the better of the two ways in reading, because the verses [end] with alif. Do you not see that (ناخرة), alongside (الحافرة) and (الساهرة), is more in keeping with the way the Revelation comes? (الناخرة) and (النخرة) are the same in meaning, like الطامع and الطمِع, and الباخل and البخِل. Some exegetes distinguished between them and said: (النخرة) is the decayed [bone], and (الناخرة) is the hollow bone through which the wind passes and makes a whistling sound (ينخر).

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا هُم بِٱلسَّاهِرَةِ﴾.
It is the face of the earth. It is as though it was given this name because the living creatures have on it their sleeping and their waking (سهرهم). [Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us], saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Ḥibbān ibn ʿAlī narrated to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: (الساهرة) is the earth; and he recited:
ففيها لحمُ ساهرةٍ وبحرٍ * ومَا فاهوُا به لهمُ مُقِيمُ
(In it is the meat of land and sea, and what they have spoken of stays with them.)

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿طُوًى﴾.
It is a valley between Medina and Egypt. Whoever declines it as a triptote says: it is a masculine [name] with which we named a masculine thing, and this is the course of what is declined. Whoever does not decline it makes it diverted (maʿdūl) [125/a] from its [original] form, as one says: رأيت عمر وذفر [Translator's note: so in the source; read زفر] ومضر, which are not declined because they are diverted from their form, as though عمر was originally عامر, and زفر was زافر, and طوى was طاوٍ. We have not found any noun from [roots with] yāʾ and wāw that was diverted from its form other than طوى; so declining it is preferable to me, since I have not found a parallel to it in diversion.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿نَكَالَ ٱلآخِرَةِ وَٱلأُوْلَىٰ﴾.
One of the two utterances is his saying: ﴿مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُمْ مِّنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرِى﴾ and the other is his saying: ﴿أَنَا رَبُّكُم الأعْلَى﴾ (24).
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَأَخَذَهُ ٱللَّهُ نَكَالَ ٱلآخِرَةِ وَٱلأُوْلَىٰ﴾.
That is: Allah seized him with a seizing that was an exemplary punishment (nakāl) for the last and the first.

farraa:27-27.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿أَأَنتُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقاً أَمِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ﴾.
He means the people of Mecca. Then He described the sky and said: He built it.

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَغْطَشَ لَيْلَهَا﴾: He made its night dark.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحَاهَا﴾: its light and its daytime.

farraa:30-30.t: His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَٱلأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ دَحَاهَا﴾. Putting الأرض in the accusative or the nominative is permissible; the accusative is more common in the reading of the readers. It is like His saying: ﴿وَالْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْنَاهُ مَنازِلَ﴾, along with many parallels in the Qur'an.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَتَاعاً لَّكُمْ﴾.
He created that as a benefit for you and an enjoyment for you. If it had been متاعٌ لكم (nominative), it would be correct, as they said: ﴿لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إِلاَّ سَاعَةً مِّنْ نَهَارٍ بَلاَغٌ﴾, and as He said: ﴿مَتَاعٌ قَلِيلٌ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾; that is on resumption (istiʾnāf), with something implied for it that puts it in the nominative.

farraa:34-34.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا جَآءَتِ ٱلطَّآمَّةُ﴾.
It is the Resurrection, which overwhelms (تطمّ) everything. One says تَطِمّ and تطُمّ, two dialectal forms.

farraa:39-41.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ هِيَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ﴾.
The abode of those of this description. Likewise His saying: ﴿فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَنَّةَ هِيَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ﴾:
the abode of the one whom We have described with what We described him — fear of his Lord and his restraining [125/b] his soul from its desire.

farraa:42-42.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَيَّانَ مُرْسَاهَا﴾.
Someone may say: anchoring (الإرساء) belongs only to the ship, the mountains and the like; so how is the Hour described with anchoring? I said: it is like the ship which, when it was moving, came to anchor; and its anchoring is its standing (قيامها). Its standing is not like the standing of one who stands on his foot and the like; it is only like your saying: justice has been established (قام العدل) and truth has been established (قام الحق), i.e. it has appeared and become firm.

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُنذِرُ مَن يَخْشَاهَا﴾.
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it in annexation (iḍāfa), while Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif and some of the people of Medina added tanwīn and said: "منذرٌ من يخشاها". Both are correct. It is like His saying: "بَالِغٌ أَمْرَه" and "بَالِغُ أمْرِه", and "مُوهِنٌ كَيْدَ الْكافِرِين" and ﴿موهنُ كيدِ الكَافرِينَ﴾, along with parallels to it in the Qur'an.

farraa:46-46.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿إِلاَّ عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحَاهَا﴾.
Someone may say: Does the evening (العشي) have a forenoon (ضحا)? The forenoon belongs only to the beginning of the day. This is clear and evident in the speech of the Arabs, that they say: آتيك العشيةَ أو غداتَها (I will come to you in the evening or its morning), and آتيك الغداةَ أو عشيتَها (I will come to you in the morning or its evening). العشية carries the meaning of "last" and الغداة the meaning of "first". One of Banū ʿUqayl recited to me:
نحن صبحنا عامراً فى دارها * عشية الهلال أو سَرارِها
(We attacked [the tribe of] ʿĀmir at dawn in their abode, on the evening of the new moon or of its last night.)
He meant: the evening of the new moon or the evening of the سَرار of the evening [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense is "the evening of its سرار", the last night of the month]. This is more forceful than آتيك الغداة أو عشيتها.
